attempts.raw_response: Specify the format, such as DVD, Blu-ray, or streaming service, immediately after the performers. If you accessed the video through an online platform, include the name of the website or service. For instance: "Citizen Kane. Dir. Orson Welles. Perfs. Orson Welles, Joseph Cotten. DVD, Warner Home Video, 2011." When citing a streaming version, you might write: "Citizen Kane. Dir. Orson Welles. Perfs. Orson Welles, Joseph Cotten. HBO Max, 2023." Be sure to include the year of the specific version or release you watched, as this helps readers locate the exact edition. If no director or producer is listed, begin with the title and move directly to the performers or other available information. Consistency across all video citations in your paper is essential for clarity and professionalism.

pair.human_continuation: For example: "Frankenstein. Dir. James Whale. Perfs. Boris Karloff, Colin Clive, Mae Clark. 1931. DVD." Generally, you need to provide enough information that your reader could follow in your footsteps and view the same video you did. The type of information you include will vary depending on how you accessed the video and how much information is available to you.  If you viewed a subsequent edition of the original video recording, include the date the video you watched was produced. For example: "Frankenstein. Dir. James Whale. Perfs. Boris Karloff, Colin Clive, Mae Clark. 1931. DVD. Universal Pictures, 2006." If you accessed the video online, you'll need to provide the name of the website where the video appears, the date you accessed it, and a direct URL to the video.
